summary: Josh Lloyd and Benjamin Garcia of Locked On Suns preview the 2026/27 Phoenix Suns. Phoenix surprised people with 45 wins last season. The second half fell apart when injuries piled up and several players coming off career years regressed at the same time. Offseason moves: they traded for Miles Bridges, added Luke Kennard, and re-signed Collin Gillespie, Jordan Goodwin and Mark Williams. Grayson Allen and Royce O'Neale left. The projected starters are Devin Booker, Jalen Green, Dillon Brooks, Miles Bridges and Mark Williams. The team wants Green to play point guard, which both hosts doubt. Ben expects Khaman Maluach to take over as starting center by late November because Williams keeps getting hurt. He sets the win total at about 41 and thinks the team takes a step back. For fantasy, Josh says bench guards like Gillespie lose minutes once the starters are healthy. He calls Maluach a reasonable flyer with role risk.

rules.text: When many players on one team have career years at once, expect some of them to regress to the mean, often all at the same time.
rules.quote: having career years that someone was going to revert back to the mean

rules.text: Fans and media tend to treat a team-wide hot streak as the new normal and ignore that it will likely come crashing back.
rules.quote: when everyone gets hot it's all celebrated and everyone thinks well this

rules.text: Teams usually try the option that protects ego, salary, draft pedigree or trade capital first. They only make harder rotation changes after it clearly fails.
rules.quote: draft pedigree which holds a lot or you know trade capital invested in players that requires

rules.text: Bench players who put up numbers in big minutes during injuries should be valued closer to their healthy-team role. Expect a rank around 150th unless something changes.
rules.quote: I've got to be okay with them being the 150th best player unless something happens

rules.text: Taking flyers on players with an uncertain role is fine. Know what has to happen for them to pay off, and drop them at the right time.
rules.quote: understanding what it takes to get there and then pulling the pin on them at the right time is a key part of having success

rules.text: Players who put up big scoring numbers only when injuries push their usage up tend to produce much less when asked to scale back.
rules.quote: he's got to ramp his usage to 28. He just scores 24 points a game because no one else can do it

player_notes.text: The Suns do not want Booker to be the primary point guard. They want to lower his ballhandling load and make spacing easier for him.
player_notes.quote: They don't want Deon Booker to uh be the point guard. They don't want that.

player_notes.text: Booker had a down year last season. Defenses rolled coverages to him and sent extra bodies, preferring to let Dillon Brooks beat them.
player_notes.quote: Devin Booker had a down year and a part of that is okay we're just going to roll our coverages

player_notes.text: Ben calls Booker an average defender who is not a net negative. He is better than people give him credit for but not good.
player_notes.quote: Devin Booker is a much better defender than people give him credit for. not a good defender

player_notes.text: The Suns want Green to be their point guard and bring the ball up. It is a big year for him.
player_notes.quote: I know that to be the case that they want Jaylen Green to be the point guard of this team.

player_notes.text: Josh says Green is a worse passer than Gillespie, has a lower basketball IQ, and has never shown point guard skills.
player_notes.quote: who's got no experience playing point guard, has never shown point guard skills in Jaylen Green.

player_notes.text: Green plays downhill but is not efficient around the rim. Ben does not trust his playmaking.
player_notes.quote: The problem is neither of those guys are efficient around the rim.

player_notes.text: Brooks was having a career year but collapsed late. He shot about 38% from the field over the final two months. He is projected to start.
player_notes.quote: Dylan Brooks shooting like 38% over the final like two months of the season

player_notes.text: Brooks has a good defensive reputation. Josh calls him the only clearly above-average defender in the projected starting group.
player_notes.quote: there's Dylan Brooks who's you got a pretty good defensive reputation

player_notes.text: Gillespie re-signed for 4 years and $40M. Ben had projected 4 years and $50M.
player_notes.quote: Colin Gillespie four years 40 million. I thought I my projection

player_notes.text: Ben thinks Gillespie should start over Jalen Green. He says Gillespie shoots threes better, handles the ball better and defends better, but the team will start Green.
player_notes.quote: Colin Gillespie into the starting lineup who a shoots the three-point ball much more effectively than Jaylen Green

player_notes.text: Gillespie played almost 29 minutes a game overall. That fell to about 23 once Green, Brooks and Booker were all back. Josh says to expect him as roughly the 150th best player unless something changes.
player_notes.quote: Colin Glesby played almost 29 minutes a game, but when we saw players return

player_notes.text: Williams does not play enough games. Even with load management, minutes limits and skipped back-to-backs, he only played 60 games.
player_notes.quote: just doesn't play games. Like he just doesn't play enough games.

player_notes.text: Ben expects Williams to get hurt, lose the starting job to Maluach, and become a backup big playing 16 to 17 minutes a night.
player_notes.quote: Mark Williams is going to play as as he should 16 17 minutes a night

player_notes.text: Williams re-signed at about $13M a year. Ben thinks the deal was mainly so the team can trade him in a year or at the deadline.
player_notes.quote: the resigning of him I believe was more about we'll move him in a year or we'll move him at the deadline

player_notes.text: Williams lives around the rim. That clogs the paint for the downhill drivers Green and Bridges.
player_notes.quote: And who likes to live around the rim? Mark Williams.

player_notes.text: Ben predicts Maluach starts by late November once Williams gets hurt. He calls Maluach a better defender who stretches the floor better.
player_notes.quote: starter of this team by late November because at some point unfortunately Mark Williams is going to get injured.

player_notes.text: Josh says Maluach is worth a fantasy flyer. If Williams plays the first 50 games, Maluach could be stuck as a 16-minute player.
player_notes.quote: It's worth taking a flyer on, but if Williams plays the first 50 games

player_notes.text: Ighodaro put up big numbers at the end of last season while Williams had a foot issue.
player_notes.quote: the guy that was putting up the big numbers at the end of last season where Williams was having the foot issue was Ogdara

player_notes.text: Ighodaro is expected to be the small-ball five, sometimes paired with Maluach.
player_notes.quote: Oso, he is clearly for small ball. He is going to be the small ball five.

player_notes.text: Ighodaro has no shooting beyond five feet. He is a smart passer, can put the ball on the floor, and is a very underrated defender.
player_notes.quote: he has got no semblance of an offensive game when it comes to shooting the ball outside of five feet

player_notes.text: Bridges shot 33% from three last year. His athleticism has declined a lot over the last three years.
player_notes.quote: his athleticism has declined significantly over the last 3 years

player_notes.text: Josh says Bridges does not generate steals or blocks, can't shoot, and passes poorly.
player_notes.quote: He doesn't generate steals or blocks and he's not as athletic as he used to be.

player_notes.text: Bridges' production has mostly come when LaMelo Ball and Brandon Miller were injured and his usage went up. His minutes shrank late last season when he was asked to scale back.
player_notes.quote: we saw his minutes actually scale down towards the end of last season as well

player_notes.text: Bridges is the projected starting power forward. The Suns hope his ball handling, rim pressure and better catch-and-shoot threes take pressure off Booker.
player_notes.quote: They love his ability to handle the ball.

player_notes.text: Ben describes Bridges as at best an inconsistent defender.
player_notes.quote: At best, he's an inconsistent defender.

player_notes.text: Ben expects Kennard to shoot about 40 to 41% from three on around eight attempts a game off the bench. That is a lower percentage on more volume.
player_notes.quote: I think Luke Canard is gonna shoot 41 40% from three, but he's gonna be asked to chuck up like eight of them a game coming off the bench.

player_notes.text: Kennard is a pure three-point shooter who historically takes too few threes. He does not get to the rim and is not a mid-range shooter.
player_notes.quote: He doesn't really get to the rim. He's not really a mid-range shooter.

player_notes.text: Allen plays bigger than his size and drives downhill, which has worn his body down. Ben thinks he has peaked and is starting the back nine of his career.
player_notes.quote: I think he reached this peak and he's probably going to start hitting the back nine of his career.

player_notes.text: O'Neale showed signs of decline. He and Allen were seen as negative assets around the league.
player_notes.quote: Royce O'Neal showed signs of that

player_notes.text: Goodwin re-signed for 3 years and $19M, which Ben calls a steal.
player_notes.quote: Three years $19 million and Jordan Goodwin is is a steal.

player_notes.text: Josh names Fleming as a possible alternative at forward if he takes a big step forward.
player_notes.quote: unless like you know Rashier Fleming takes a big step forward and he's able to move into a role.

team_notes.text: The projected starting lineup is Devin Booker, Jalen Green, Dillon Brooks, Miles Bridges and Mark Williams.
team_notes.quote: Deon Booker, Jaylen Green, Dylan Brooks, Miles Bridges, and then Mark Williams.

team_notes.text: Phoenix was one of the worst teams in the NBA by record in the second half of last season after injuries and regression.
team_notes.quote: you saw the Suns be actually one of the worst teams in the NBA record-wise in the second half of the season

team_notes.text: Ben worries the starting lineup has no reliable three-point shooting. The team believes more ball handlers will create open threes.
team_notes.quote: which one of those guys is going to hit an open three-point shot, Josh? Which one? That's none of them.

team_notes.text: Ben sets the win total at about 41, with a range from about 35 to 50. He expects a step back.
team_notes.quote: I'm like right at 41 wins. I think there is a world where this team could win 50 games

team_notes.text: Ben expects the defense to rank around 13th or 14th after a top 10 finish last year.
team_notes.quote: I think right now they're like 13th, 14th because they do have guys who are going to try really hard

team_notes.text: Owner Matt Ishbia runs the organization and handles the contracts. The front office prefers re-signing its own players on cheap deals over free agency.
team_notes.quote: This is a Matt Ishbia ran organization. This is not a Brian Gregory run organization.

team_notes.text: The center rotation of Williams, Maluach and Ighodaro is crowded and unclear. Ben expects Williams' injuries to open minutes.
team_notes.quote: Mark Williams is just going to be injured. So it's not going to be that hard to find minutes

team_notes.text: After one of their best seasons in a long time, the Hornets chose to move Miles Bridges rather than pay him.
team_notes.quote: Hornets just had one of their best seasons in a long time. Like most successful seasons.

claims_to_check.text: Phoenix won 45 games last season against a preseason win total of 31.5.
claims_to_check.quote: Last year was 31 and a half. They they won all they won 45 games.

claims_to_check.text: Mark Williams averaged about 23 minutes per game last season, his lowest since his rookie year, and played 60 games.
claims_to_check.quote: 23 minutes, the least of his career since his rookie season. And he still could not stay healthy.

claims_to_check.text: Mark Williams set a career high of about 1,400 total minutes last season, nearly 400 more than his previous high of about 1,100.
claims_to_check.quote: He played the most minutes of his career last season like in terms of total minutes by like almost 400 minutes.

claims_to_check.quote: The guy that shot 33% from three last year.
